title: The committed autopilot digest carries the tick's own lines, as the autopilot skill says it does
goal: kbdecide.py digest --commit writes, beside the unratified decisions, the last tick's actions from _cache/autopilot/state.json or ticks.jsonl: runners started and ended with their causes, sprints refused as operator-present only, bounds stops, kept gates left open, steps skipped; the skill's step 7 promises these lines and step 8 sends errors, refusals and finished sprints to the digest only, but digest_text writes decisions and the disagreement figures alone, so an unattended operator learns none of them
notes: Theme: how an unattended manager communicates. Evidence: kbdecide.py:652-673 digest_text writes the decisions and the disagreement figures only; kb-autopilot SKILL.md:34 (step 7) and :35 (step 8: errors, finished sprints and refused commands wait in the committed digest). The fleet used free-text messages and status asks for the same facts (mac-third, mac-fifth feedback).
